name: Resize Text
explanation: This criterion requires that text can be resized up to 200% of its default size, using the browser's own zoom feature, without losing content or functionality. At 200% zoom, every piece of text must still be readable and every control must still be usable. Nothing should be clipped off by a fixed-size container, overlap other elements, or force horizontal scrolling to read a single line. The page layout is expected to reflow — text wrapping onto more lines, containers growing taller, sections stacking — rather than staying rigid and cutting things off. The one exception is captions and images of text, which aren't required to resize this way. This is purely about zoom working correctly; it says nothing about font choice or default size.
whoItAffects: People with low vision who don't use a screen reader but do rely on enlarged text to read comfortably — a much larger population than screen reader users. It affects older adults with presbyopia or other common age-related vision changes who zoom their browser as a matter of habit. It also affects anyone with a temporary or situational limitation, like reading on a phone at arm's length or in bright glare, who reaches for the zoom controls rather than turning on specialized software. When zoom breaks a layout, these users lose access to content or controls entirely, not just find them harder to read.
howToTest: In your browser, zoom in until you reach 200%. Then go through the page. Read every paragraph and label to confirm no text is cut off, hidden, or overlapping. Check that buttons, form fields, and links are still fully visible and clickable rather than crushed together. Confirm you never have to scroll horizontally to read a single line of text — some horizontal scrolling for wide elements like data tables is fine, but body text should reflow, not truncate. Also check that pinch-to-zoom works on a touchscreen device and isn't blocked by the page.

check.question: A page's viewport meta tag includes `user-scalable=no`, which prevents visitors from zooming in on mobile browsers at all. What does this cause with respect to SC 1.4.4 Resize Text?
choices: No failure, because SC 1.4.4 only applies to desktop browsers, not mobile
No failure, because disabling zoom is only a problem if the site also uses small fonts
A failure, because it prevents users from resizing text up to 200% using the browser's native zoom
A failure, but only if the page also uses fixed-height containers with overflow: hidden
